Every route here requires a signed-in user.\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nfrom fastapi import APIRouter, Request\n\nfrom app import auth\nfrom app.templating import templates\n\nrouter = APIRouter()\n\n\n@router.get(\"/admin\")\ndef admin_home(request: Request, user=auth.SIGNED_IN):\n    return templates.TemplateResponse(\n        request, \"admin/hello.html\", {\"title\": \"Admin\", \"user\": user},\n    )\n=== app/main.py\n\"\"\"The FastAPI application.\n\nThe admin console answers at /admin (behind login) and the public preview at /.\nRoutes live in their own modules under app/routes/ and are included here. Keep\nthis file small.\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nfrom fastapi import FastAPI, Request\nfrom fastapi.responses import HTMLResponse, RedirectResponse\nfrom starlette.middleware.sessions import SessionMiddleware\n\nfrom app import auth, settings\nfrom app.publish import render_home\nfrom app.routes import admin, login, updates\nfrom app.templating import templates\n\n\ndef create_app() -> FastAPI:\n    app = FastAPI(title=\"IPHS 400 MP2 CMS\")\n    app.add_middleware(SessionMiddleware, secret_key=settings.SECRET_KEY,\n                       session_cookie=\"cms_session\", same_site=\"strict\")\n\n    @app.exception_handler(auth.LoginRequired)\n    def send_to_login(request: Request, exc: auth.LoginRequired):\n        return RedirectResponse(\"/login\", status_code=303)\n\n    @app.exception_handler(auth.Refused)\n    def refused_screen(request: Request, exc: auth.Refused):\n        return templates.TemplateResponse(\n            request, \"admin/refused.html\",\n            {\"title\": \"Not allowed\", \"reason\": exc.detail,\n             \"user\": auth.signed_in_user(request)},\n            status_code=403,\n        )\n\n    app.include_router(login.router)\n    app.include_router(admin.router)\n    app.include_router(updates.router)\n\n    @app.get(\"/\", response_class=HTMLResponse)\n    def public_home():\n        # A quick look at the home page. The full site, with its stylesheet\n        # and update pages, is what `cms publish` writes to site/.\n        return render_home()\n\n    return app\n\n\napp = create_app()\n=== app/templating.py\n\"\"\"The Jinja environment shared by the admin console routes.\n\nEvery admin template gets `csrf_token`, so each state-changing form can carry\nit without each route passing it by hand, and `flash`, the one-time message a\nroute left with flash() before redirecting.\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nfrom fastapi import Request\nfrom fastapi.templating import Jinja2Templates\n\nfrom app import auth, settings\n\n\ndef flash(request: Request, kind: str, text: str) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Leave a message (\"success\" or \"error\") for the next page rendered.\"\"\"\n    request.session[\"flash\"] = {\"kind\": kind, \"text\": text}\n\n\ndef _csrf(request: Request) -> dict[str, str]:\n    return {\"csrf_token\": auth.csrf_token(request)}\n\n\ndef _flash(request: Request) -> dict[str, dict | None]:\n    return {\"flash\": request.session.pop(\"flash\", None)}\n\n\ntemplates = Jinja2Templates(directory=str(settings.TEMPLATES),\n                            context_processors=[_csrf, _flash])\n=== app/markdown.py\n\"\"\"User Markdown -> safe HTML.\n\nEvery place that shows a body (the admin preview now, the export later) goes\nthrough render(), so there is one sanitizer and one allow-list.\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport nh3\nfrom markdown_it import MarkdownIt\n\n_md = MarkdownIt(\"commonmark\")\n\n# Links may only point at the web or an email address; anything else\n# (javascript:, data:, ...) is dropped by nh3.\n_URL_SCHEMES = {\"http\", \"https\", \"mailto\"}\n\n\ndef render(body: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Render Markdown and strip every tag and attribute not on nh3's allow-list.\"\"\"\n    return nh3.clean(_md.render(body), url_schemes=_URL_SCHEMES)\n=== app/cli.py\n\"\"\"The `cms` command: serve, publish, deploy.\n\n    uv run cms serve      # admin console + public preview at http://localhost:8000\n    uv run cms publish    # render site/ from published content\n    uv run cms deploy     # push site/ to the gh-pages branch (Pages serves it)\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport argparse\nimport subprocess\nimport sys\n\nfrom app import settings\nfrom app.publish import render_site\n\n\ndef main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:\n    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog=\"cms\")\n    sub = parser.add_subparsers(dest=\"command\", required=True)\n    serve = sub.add_parser(\"serve\", help=\"run the admin console locally\")\n    serve.add_argument(\"--port\", type=int, default=8000)\n    serve.add_argument(\"--reload\", action=\"store_true\", default=True)\n    sub.add_parser(\"publish\", help=\"render site/ from published content\")\n    deploy = sub.add_parser(\"deploy\", help=\"push site/ to gh-pages\")\n    deploy.add_argument(\"--message\", default=\"Publish site\")\n    args = parser.parse_args(argv)\n\n    if args.command == \"serve\":\n        import uvicorn\n\n        uvicorn.run(\"app.main:app\", port=args.port, reload=args.reload)\n        return 0\n\n    if args.command == \"publish\":\n        out = render_site()\n        print(f\"Wrote {out}. Preview it with:  python3 -m http.server -d {out} 8001\")\n        return 0\n\n    if args.command == \"deploy\":\n        if not settings.SITE.exists():\n            print(\"site/ does not exist yet — run `uv run cms publish` first.\")\n            return 1\n        result = subprocess.run(\n            [sys.executable, \"-m\", \"ghp_import\", \"-n\", \"-p\", \"-m\", args.message,\n             str(settings.SITE)],\n        )\n        if result.returncode == 0:\n            print(\"Pushed to gh-pages. Settings -> Pages -> Deploy from a branch -> \"\n                  \"gh-pages / root, then wait up to 10 minutes.\")\n        return result.returncode\n    return 1\n\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    raise SystemExit(main())","is_error":false}]},"uuid":"46e581a4-1c08-48c0-b331-00707e2d355e","timestamp":"2026-10-13T14:04:20.746Z","toolUseResult":{"stdout":"=== app/db.py\n\"\"\"SQLite access. Every call opens a short-lived connection to the current\nsettings.DATABASE_PATH, so tests can point it at a temporary file.\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport sqlite3\nfrom contextlib import contextmanager\nfrom collections.abc import Iterator\n\nfrom app import settings\n\nSCHEMA = \"\"\"\nCREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS users (\n    id            INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,\n    email         TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE COLLATE NOCASE,\n    name          TEXT NOT NULL,\n    password_hash TEXT NOT NULL,\n    role          TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (role IN ('admin', 'editor')),\n    active        INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1,\n    created_at    TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP\n);\n\n-- An Update is stored as a post (see CONTEXT.md).\nCREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS posts (\n    id         INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,\n    title      TEXT NOT NULL,\n    slug       TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,\n    body       TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',\n    status     TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'draft' CHECK (status IN ('draft', 'published')),\n    author_id  INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES users (id),\n    created_at TEXT NOT NULL,\n    updated_at TEXT NOT NULL\n);\n\"\"\"\n\n\n@contextmanager\ndef connect() -> Iterator[sqlite3.Connection]:\n    \"\"\"Yield a connection with the schema in place; commit on success.\"\"\"\n    conn = sqlite3.connect(settings.DATABASE_PATH)\n    conn.row_factory = sqlite3.Row\n    try:\n        conn.executescript(SCHEMA)\n        yield conn\n        conn.commit()\n    finally:\n        conn.close()\n=== app/updates.py\n\"\"\"Updates: team news items, stored as posts.\n\nNew updates are always drafts. The slug is made from the title on first save,\nkept unique, and never changed by an edit.\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport re\nimport sqlite3\nimport unicodedata\nfrom datetime import datetime, timezone\n\nfrom app import db\n\n\nclass InvalidUpdate(ValueError):\n    \"\"\"The form cannot be saved; the message is shown to the user.\"\"\"\n\n\n_SELECT = (\n    \"SELECT posts.id, title, slug, body, status, posts.created_at, updated_at, \"\n    \"posts.author_id, users.name AS author FROM posts JOIN users ON users.id = posts.author_id\"\n)\n\n\ndef slugify(title: str) -> str:\n    # Strip accents (é -> e); any other non-ASCII character separates words.\n    plain = \"\".join(c for c in unicodedata.normalize(\"NFKD\", title)\n                    if not unicodedata.combining(c))\n    return re.sub(r\"[^a-z0-9]+\", \"-\", plain.lower()).strip(\"-\") or \"update\"\n\n\ndef _unique_slug(conn: sqlite3.Connection, title: str) -> str:\n    base = slugify(title)\n    taken = {row[\"slug\"] for row in conn.execute(\n        \"SELECT slug FROM posts WHERE slug = ? OR slug LIKE ?\", (base, f\"{base}-%\"))}\n    slug, n = base, 2\n    while slug in taken:\n        slug, n = f\"{base}-{n}\", n + 1\n    return slug\n\n\ndef _now() -> str:\n    return datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(timespec=\"seconds\")\n\n\ndef _clean_title(title: str) -> str:\n    title = title.strip()\n    if not title:\n        raise InvalidUpdate(\"The title cannot be empty.\")\n    return title\n\n\ndef create_update(title: str, body: str, author_id: int) -> int:\n    title = _clean_title(title)\n    now = _now()\n    with db.connect() as conn:\n        cursor = conn.execute(\n            \"INSERT INTO posts (title, slug, body, status, author_id, created_at, updated_at) \"\n            \"VALUES (?, ?, ?, 'draft', ?, ?, ?)\",\n            (title, _unique_slug(conn, title), body, author_id, now, now),\n        )\n        return cursor.lastrowid\n\n\ndef edit_update(update_id: int, title: str, body: str) -> None:\n    title = _clean_title(title)\n    with db.connect() as conn:\n        conn.execute(\n            \"UPDATE posts SET title = ?, body = ?, updated_at = ? WHERE id = ?\",\n            (title, body, _now(), update_id),\n        )\n\n\ndef publish(update_id: int) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Mark published. Going live counts as an update, so fans see a fresh date.\"\"\"\n    with db.connect() as conn:\n        conn.execute(\"UPDATE posts SET status = 'published', updated_at = ? WHERE id = ?\",\n                     (_now(), update_id))\n\n\ndef unpublish(update_id: int) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Back to draft. The next `cms publish` removes it from the site.\"\"\"\n    with db.connect() as conn:\n        conn.execute(\"UPDATE posts SET status = 'draft' WHERE id = ?\", (update_id,))\n\n\ndef delete_update(update_id: int) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Gone for good. If it was published, the next `cms publish` removes it.\"\"\"\n    with db.connect() as conn:\n        conn.execute(\"DELETE FROM posts WHERE id = ?\", (update_id,))\n\n\ndef get_update(update_id: int) -> sqlite3.Row | None:\n    with db.connect() as conn:\n        return conn.execute(f\"{_SELECT} WHERE posts.id = ?\", (update_id,)).fetchone()\n\n\ndef list_published() -> list[sqlite3.Row]:\n    \"\"\"What `cms publish` exports: published updates, newest written first.\n\n    Ordered by created_at, not updated_at, so a correction never jumps above a\n    newer update (CONTEXT.md, Decisions).\"\"\"\n    with db.connect() as conn:\n        return conn.execute(f\"{_SELECT} WHERE status = 'published' \"\n                            \"ORDER BY posts.created_at DESC, posts.id DESC\").fetchall()\n\n\ndef list_updates() -> list[sqlite3.Row]:\n    with db.connect() as conn:\n        return conn.execute(f\"{_SELECT} ORDER BY updated_at DESC, posts.id DESC\").fetchall()\n=== app/permissions.py\n\"\"\"Who may change which update (spec #1, Permissions).\n\nThe admin may do anything. An editor may edit any draft and delete only their\nown drafts; published updates are the admin's alone. The `may_*` functions\nanswer for templates; the `check_*` functions raise Refused for routes, and\nthe refused screen shows the reason.\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport sqlite3\n\nfrom app.auth import Refused\n\nPUBLISHED_IS_ADMIN_ONLY = (\"This update is published, so only the admin can change or \"\n                           \"delete it. Editors can edit drafts only.\")\nOWN_DRAFTS_ONLY = \"Editors can delete only their own drafts. Ask the author or the admin.\"\n\n\ndef is_admin(user: sqlite3.Row) -> bool:\n    return user[\"role\"] == \"admin\"\n\n\ndef may_edit(user: sqlite3.Row, update: sqlite3.Row) -> bool:\n    return is_admin(user) or update[\"status\"] == \"draft\"\n\n\ndef may_delete(user: sqlite3.Row, update: sqlite3.Row) -> bool:\n    return is_admin(user) or (update[\"status\"] == \"draft\"\n                              and update[\"author_id\"] == user[\"id\"])\n\n\ndef check_edit(user: sqlite3.Row, update: sqlite3.Row) -> None:\n    if not may_edit(user, update):\n        raise Refused(PUBLISHED_IS_ADMIN_ONLY)\n\n\ndef check_delete(user: sqlite3.Row, update: sqlite3.Row) -> None:\n    check_edit(user, update)\n    if not may_delete(user, update):\n        raise Refused(OWN_DRAFTS_ONLY)\n=== app/publish.py\n\"\"\"Render the public site into site/ as plain HTML.\n\nTwo rules the rubric checks:\n\n  1. var(--purple) 60%, #6a4bb0);\n  border-bottom: .4rem solid #fff; box-shadow: 0 .4rem 0 var(--purple);\n  padding: 1.5rem 1rem; text-align: center;\n}\n.banner a { color: #fff; font-size: 1.6rem; font-weight: 800; letter-spacing: .02em;\n            text-decoration: none; text-transform: uppercase; }\nmain, footer { margin: 0 auto; max-width: 42rem; padding: 0 1rem; }\nmain { margin-block: 2rem; overflow-wrap: anywhere; }\nh1, h2, h3 { color: var(--purple-dark); line-height: 1.25; }\na { color: var(--purple); }\n.updates { list-style: none; padding: 0; }\n.updates li { border-left: .3rem solid var(--purple); background: var(--lilac);\n              margin-bottom: .75rem; padding: .6rem .9rem; }\n.updates a { display: block; font-weight: 700; }\n.meta, small { color: #5a5266; }\nimg, video { max-width: 100%; height: auto; }\npre { overflow-x: auto; }\ntable { display: block; overflow-x: auto; }\nfooter { border-top: 2px solid var(--lilac); padding-block: 1rem; }\n\"\"\"\n\n# Dates on the public site are the team's local date, not UTC: an update saved\n# at 9 pm Eastern is already \"tomorrow\" in UTC.\nLOCAL_TIME = ZoneInfo(\"America/New_York\")\n\n\ndef local_date(timestamp: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"'2026-10-13T01:30:00+00:00' -> 'October 12, 2026'.\"\"\"\n    local = datetime.fromisoformat(timestamp).astimezone(LOCAL_TIME)\n    return f\"{local:%B} {local.day}, {local.year}\"\n\n\ndef update_path(update) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Where an update's page lives, relative to the site root.\"\"\"\n    return f\"updates/{update['slug']}.html\"\n\n\ndef environment() -> Environment:\n    env = Environment(\n        loader=FileSystemLoader(str(settings.TEMPLATES)),\n        autoescape=select_autoescape([\"html\"]),\n    )\n    env.filters[\"local_date\"] = local_date\n    env.globals[\"site_title\"] = settings.SITE_TITLE\n    return env\n\n\ndef render_site(out: Path | None = None) -> Path:\n    out = out or settings.SITE\n out\n\n\ndef render_home(published: list | None = None, env: Environment | None = None) -> str:\n    \"\"\"The home page: published updates, newest first, each with its date.\"\"\"\n    if published update_id: int, user=auth.SIGNED_IN):\n    update = get_or_404(update_id)\n    return editor_page(request, user, update=update,\n                       title=update[\"title\"], body=update[\"body\"])\n\n\n@router.post(\"/{update_id}\")\ndef save_update(request: Request, update_id: int, user=auth.SIGNED_IN, _csrf=auth.CSRF,\n                title: str = Form(\"\"), body: str = Form(\"\"), action: str = Form(\"save\")):\n    update = get_or_404(update_id)\n    permissions.check_edit(user, update)\n    if action == \"preview\":\n        return editor_page(request, user, update=update, title=title, body=body)\n    try:\n        updates.edit_update(update_id, title, body)\n    except updates.InvalidUpdate as exc:\n        return editor_page(request, user, update=update, title=title, body=body,\n                           error=str(exc), status=400)\n    flash(request, \"success\", \"Changes saved.\")\n    return RedirectResponse(f\"/admin/updates/{update_id}\", status_code=303)\n\n\ndef change_status(request: Request, update_id: int, change, message: str):\n    get_or_404(update_id)\n    change(update_id)\n    flash(request, \"success\", message)\n    return RedirectResponse(f\"/admin/updates/{update_id}\", status_code=303)\n\n\n@router.post(\"/{update_id}/publish\")\ndef publish_update(request: Request, update_id: int, user=auth.ADMIN, _csrf=auth.CSRF):\n    return change_status(request, update_id, updates.publish,\n                         \"Published. Run cms publish and cms deploy to put it live.\")\n\n\n@router.post(\"/{update_id}/unpublish\")\ndef unpublish_update(request: Request, update_id: int, user=auth.ADMIN, _csrf=auth.CSRF):\n    return change_status(request, update_id, updates.unpublish,\n                         \"Unpublished. Run cms publish and cms deploy to take it down.\")\n\n\n@router.get(\"/{update_id}/delete\")\ndef confirm_delete(request: Request, update_id: int, user=auth.SIGNED_IN):\n    update = get_or_404(update_id)\n    permissions.check_delete(user, update)\n    return templates.TemplateResponse(\n        request, \"admin/update_delete.html\",\n        {\"title\": \"Delete update\", \"user\": user, \"update\": update},\n    )\n\n\n@router.post(\"/{update_id}/delete\")\ndef delete_update(request: Request, update_id: int, user=auth.SIGNED_IN, _csrf=auth.CSRF):\n    update = get_or_404(update_id)\n    permissions.check_delete(user, update)\n    updates.delete_update(update_id)\n    if update[\"status\"] == \"published\":\n        flash(request, \"success\", f\"Deleted “{update['title']}”. \"\n                                  \"Run cms publish and cms deploy to take it down.\")\n    else:\n        flash(request, \"success\", f\"Deleted the draft “{update['title']}”.\")\n    return RedirectResponse(\"/admin/updates\", status_code=303)\n=== app/routes/admin.py\n\"\"\"The admin console home. Every route here requires a signed-in user.\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nfrom fastapi import APIRouter, Request\n\nfrom app import auth\nfrom app.templating import templates\n\nrouter = APIRouter()\n\n\n@router.get(\"/admin\")\ndef admin_home(request: Request, user=auth.SIGNED_IN):\n    return templates.TemplateResponse(\n        request, \"admin/hello.html\", {\"title\": \"Admin\", \"user\": user},\n    )\n=== app/main.py\n\"\"\"The FastAPI application.\n\nThe admin console answers at /admin (behind login) and the public preview at /.\nRoutes live in their own modules under app/routes/ and are included here. Keep\nthis file small.\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nfrom fastapi import FastAPI, Request\nfrom fastapi.responses import HTMLResponse, RedirectResponse\nfrom starlette.middleware.sessions import SessionMiddleware\n\nfrom app import auth, settings\nfrom app.publish import render_home\nfrom app.routes import admin, login, updates\nfrom app.templating import templates\n\n\ndef create_app() -> FastAPI:\n    app = FastAPI(title=\"IPHS 400 MP2 CMS\")\n    app.add_middleware(SessionMiddleware, secret_key=settings.SECRET_KEY,\n                       session_cookie=\"cms_session\", same_site=\"strict\")\n\n    @app.exception_handler(auth.LoginRequired)\n    def send_to_login(request: Request, exc: auth.LoginRequired):\n        return RedirectResponse(\"/login\", status_code=303)\n\n    @app.exception_handler(auth.Refused)\n    def refused_screen(request: Request, exc: auth.Refused):\n        return templates.TemplateResponse(\n            request, \"admin/refused.html\",\n            {\"title\": \"Not allowed\", \"reason\": exc.detail,\n             \"user\": auth.signed_in_user(request)},\n            status_code=403,\n        )\n\n    app.include_router(login.router)\n    app.include_router(admin.router)\n    app.include_router(updates.router)\n\n    @app.get(\"/\", response_class=HTMLResponse)\n    def public_home():\n        # A quick look at the home page. The full site, with its stylesheet\n        # and update pages, is what `cms publish` writes to site/.\n        return render_home()\n\n    return app\n\n\napp = create_app()\n=== app/templating.py\n\"\"\"The Jinja environment shared by the admin console routes.\n\nEvery admin template gets `csrf_token`, so each state-changing form can carry\nit without each route passing it by hand, and `flash`, the one-time message a\nroute left with flash() before redirecting.\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nfrom fastapi import Request\nfrom fastapi.templating import Jinja2Templates\n\nfrom app import auth, settings\n\n\ndef flash(request: Request, kind: str, text: str) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Leave a message (\"success\" or \"error\") for the next page rendered.\"\"\"\n    request.session[\"flash\"] = {\"kind\": kind, \"text\": text}\n\n\ndef _csrf(request: Request) -> dict[str, str]:\n    return {\"csrf_token\": auth.csrf_token(request)}\n\n\ndef _flash(request: Request) -> dict[str, dict | None]:\n    return {\"flash\": request.session.pop(\"flash\", None)}\n\n\ntemplates = Jinja2Templates(directory=str(settings.TEMPLATES),\n                            context_processors=[_csrf, _flash])\n=== app/markdown.py\n\"\"\"User Markdown -> safe HTML.\n\nEvery place that shows a body (the admin preview now, the export later) goes\nthrough render(), so there is one sanitizer and one allow-list.\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport nh3\nfrom markdown_it import MarkdownIt\n\n_md = MarkdownIt(\"commonmark\")\n\n# Links may only point at the web or an email address; anything else\n# (javascript:, data:, ...) is dropped by nh3.\n_URL_SCHEMES = {\"http\", \"https\", \"mailto\"}\n\n\ndef render(body: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Render Markdown and strip every tag and attribute not on nh3's allow-list.\"\"\"\n    return nh3.clean(_md.render(body), url_schemes=_URL_SCHEMES)\n=== app/cli.py\n\"\"\"The `cms` command: serve, publish, deploy.\n\n    uv run cms serve      # admin console + public preview at http://localhost:8000\n    uv run cms publish    # render site/ from published content\n    uv run cms deploy     # push site/ to the gh-pages branch (Pages serves it)\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport argparse\nimport subprocess\nimport sys\n\nfrom app import settings\nfrom app.publish import render_site\n\n\ndef main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:\n    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog=\"cms\")\n    sub = parser.add_subparsers(dest=\"command\", required=True)\n    serve = sub.add_parser(\"serve\", help=\"run the admin console locally\")\n    serve.add_argument(\"--port\", type=int, default=8000)\n    serve.add_argument(\"--reload\", action=\"store_true\", default=True)\n    sub.add_parser(\"publish\", help=\"render site/ from published content\")\n    deploy = sub.add_parser(\"deploy\", help=\"push site/ to gh-pages\")\n    deploy.add_argument(\"--message\", default=\"Publish site\")\n    args = parser.parse_args(argv)\n\n    if args.command == \"serve\":\n        import uvicorn\n\n        uvicorn.run(\"app.main:app\", port=args.port, reload=args.reload)\n        return 0\n\n    if args.command == \"publish\":\n        out = render_site()\n        print(f\"Wrote {out}. Preview it with:  python3 -m http.server -d {out} 8001\")\n        return 0\n\n    if args.command == \"deploy\":\n        if not settings.SITE.exists():\n            print(\"site/ does not exist yet — run `uv run cms publish` first.\")\n            return 1\n        result = subprocess.run(\n            [sys.executable, \"-m\", \"ghp_import\", \"-n\", \"-p\", \"-m\", args.message,\n             str(settings.SITE)],\n        )\n        if result.returncode == 0:\n            print(\"Pushed to gh-pages. Settings -> Pages -> Deploy from a branch -> \"\n                  \"gh-pages / root, then wait up to 10 minutes.\")\n        return result.returncode\n    return 1\n\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    raise SystemExit(main())","stderr":"","interrupted":false,"isImage":false,"noOutputExpected":false},"serverClassifierContext":{"request":"e763f664-5de2-4cb2-b30f-545e40f59465","context":{"git_state":{"cwd":"/Users/maysg/orca/iphs400-mp2-cms","root":"/Users/maysg/orca/iphs400-mp2-cms","branch":"main","default_branch":"main","status":{"clean":false,"counts":{"staged":0,"modified":1,"untracked":null,"untracked_normal":1},"porcelain":null,"truncated":false},"visibility":{"origin":{"host":"github.com","remote":"MaysG-creator/iphs400-mp2-cms","visibility":"public"},"push_remote":"origin","remotes":[{"name":"origin","host":"github.com","remote":"MaysG-creator/iphs400-mp2-cms","visibility":"public"}],"visibility_cache":[{"host":"github.com","remote":"MaysG-creator/iphs400-mp2-cms","visibility":"public"}]}},"live_cwd":"/Users/maysg/orca/iphs400-mp2-cms","platform":"macos"}},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"685e617c-994d-4a47-ba3e-52a8df60c408","permissionDecision":{"decision":"accept","source":"config","reasonType":"classifier"},"session_id":"a121db57-1bee-4dbb-8856-8744e70c4142","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/Users/maysg/orca/iphs400-mp2-cms","sessionId":"afcf6f29-4133-4319-8044-e192682b7663","version":"2.1.296","gitBranch":"main"}

{"parentUuid":"ff973465-d6cb-4d91-ac79-534d6b35a666","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"a5562329-995b-4707-987c-82232d648936","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01G99cc2yAm9vwyhsY1MkWs9","type":"tool_result","content":"=== templates/admin/base.html\n<!doctype html>\n<html lang=\"en\">\n<head>\n  <meta charset=\"utf-8\">\n  <meta name=\"viewport\" content=\"width=device-width, initial-scale=1\">\n  <title>{{ title }} · CMS admin</title>\n  <style>\n    *, *::before, *::after { box-sizing: border-box; }\n    body { font: 16px/1.5 system-ui, sans-serif; margin: 0 auto; max-width: 48rem; padding: 1rem; }\n    nav { display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: .5rem 1rem; align-items: center;\n          border-bottom: 1px solid #ccc; padding-bottom: .5rem; }\n    nav form { margin-left: auto; }\n    label { display: block; margin-top: 1rem; }\n    input, textarea { width: 100%; max-width: 24rem; padding: .5rem; font: inherit; }\n    textarea { max-width: none; min-height: 12rem; }\n    button { margin-top: 1rem; padding: .5rem 1rem; font: inherit; }\n    nav button { margin-top: 0; }\n    .error { border: 1px solid #b00020; color: #b00020; padding: .5rem; }\n    .success { border: 1px solid #1b5e20; color: #1b5e20; padding: .5rem; }\n    .preview { border: 1px dashed #999; padding: 0 1rem; }\n    .preview img { max-width: 100%; }\n    .preview pre { overflow-x: auto; }\n    table { border-collapse: collapse; width: 100%; }\n    th, td { text-align: left; padding: .25rem .5rem .25rem 0; vertical-align: top; }\n    main { overflow-wrap: anywhere; }\n  </style>\n</head>\n<body>\n  {% if user %}\n  <nav>\n    <strong>CMS admin</strong>\n    <a href=\"{{ url_for('admin_home').path }}\">Home</a>\n    <a href=\"{{ url_for('list_updates').path }}\">Updates</a>\n    <a href=\"{{ url_for('new_update').path }}\">New update</a>\n    <span>{{ user.name }} ({{ user.email }}, {{ user.role }})</span>\n    <form method=\"post\" action=\"/logout\">\n      <input type=\"hidden\" name=\"csrf_token\" value=\"{{ csrf_token }}\">\n      <button type=\"submit\">Log out</button>\n    </form>\n  </nav>\n  {% endif %}\n  <main>\n    {% if flash %}<p class=\"{{ flash.kind }}\" role=\"status\">{{ flash.text }}</p>{% endif %}\n    {% block content %}{% endblock %}\n  </main>\n</body>\n</html>\n=== templates/admin/hello.html\n{% extends \"admin/base.html\" %}\n{% block content %}\n  <h1>T00: hello admin</h1>\n  <p>Signed in as {{ user.name }}. The dashboard arrives in a later ticket.</p>\n{% endblock %}\n=== templates/admin/login.html\n{% extends \"admin/base.html\" %}\n{% block content %}\n  <h1>Log in</h1>\n  {% if error %}<p class=\"error\" role=\"alert\">{{ error }}</p>{% endif %}\n  <form method=\"post\" action=\"/login\">\n    <input type=\"hidden\" name=\"csrf_token\" value=\"{{ csrf_token }}\">\n    <label for=\"email\">Email</label>\n    <input id=\"email\" name=\"email\" type=\"email\" value=\"{{ email }}\" autocomplete=\"username\" required autofocus>\n    <label for=\"password\">Password</label>\n    <input id=\"password\" name=\"password\" type=\"password\" autocomplete=\"current-password\" required>\n    <button type=\"submit\">Log in</button>\n  </form>\n{% endblock %}\n=== templates/admin/refused.html\n{% extends \"admin/base.html\" %}\n{% block content %}\n  <h1>Not allowed</h1>\n  <p class=\"error\" role=\"alert\">{{ reason }}</p>\n  <p>Editors write updates, edit any draft, and delete their own drafts.\n     Only the admin publishes, unpublishes, and changes or deletes published content.</p>\n  {% if user %}<p><a href=\"{{ url_for('list_updates').path }}\">Back to updates</a></p>{% endif %}\n{% endblock %}\n=== templates/admin/update_delete.html\n{% extends \"admin/base.html\" %}\n{% block content %}\n  <h1>Delete “{{ update.title }}”?</h1>\n  {% if update.status == \"published\" %}\n  <p class=\"error\" role=\"alert\">This update is published. Deleting it removes it from the\n     public site at the next <code>cms publish</code> and <code>cms deploy</code>.</p>\n  {% endif %}\n  <p>This cannot be undone.</p>\n  <form method=\"post\" response.status_code == 303\n    assert response.headers[\"location\"].endswith(\"/login\")\n=== app/auth.py\n\"\"\"Sessions, CSRF tokens, and the signed-in user.\n\nThe session lives in a signed cookie (Starlette's SessionMiddleware). It holds\nonly the user id and the CSRF token, never a password.\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport hmac\nimport secrets\nimport sqlite3\n\nfrom fastapi import Depends, HTTPException, Request\n\nfrom app import users\n\n\nclass LoginRequired(Exception):\n    \"\"\"Raised for an anonymous visitor; main.py turns it into a redirect.\"\"\"\n\n\nclass Refused(HTTPException):\n    \"\"\"A signed-in user tried something their role does not allow. main.py\n    shows the \"not allowed\" screen with this reason, as a 403.\"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self, reason: str):\n        super().__init__(status_code=403, detail=reason)\n\n\ndef csrf_token(request: Request) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Return this session's CSRF token, creating one if needed.\"\"\"\n    token = request.session.get(\"csrf_token\")\n    if not token:\n        token = secrets.token_urlsafe(32)\n        request.session[\"csrf_token\"] = token\n    return token\n\n\nasync def check_csrf(request: Request) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Dependency for every state-changing route: reject a missing or wrong token.\"\"\"\n    form = await request.form()\n    sent = form.get(\"csrf_token\")\n    expected = request.session.get(\"csrf_token\")\n    if not (isinstance(sent, str) and expected\n            and hmac.compare_digest(sent, expected)):\n        raise HTTPException(status_code=403, detail=\"Invalid or missing CSRF token\")\n\n\ndef signed_in_user(request: Request) -> sqlite3.Row | None:\n    \"\"\"The signed-in, still-active user, or None.\"\"\"\n    user_id = request.session.get(\"user_id\")\n    return users.get_active_user(user_id) if user_id else None\n\n\ndef current_user(request: Request) -> sqlite3.Row:\n    \"\"\"Dependency for every admin screen: the signed-in, still-active user.\"\"\"\n    user = signed_in_user(request)\n    if user is None:\n        request.session.pop(\"user_id\", None)\n        raise LoginRequired\n    return user\n\n\ndef admin_user(user: sqlite3.Row = Depends(current_user)) -> sqlite3.Row:\n    \"\"\"Dependency for admin-only actions: an editor is refused with 403.\"\"\"\n    if user[\"role\"] != \"admin\":\n        raise Refused(\"Only the admin can do this.\")\n    return user\n\n\ndef start_session(request: Request, user: sqlite3.Row) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Begin a fresh session for the user, with a new CSRF token.\"\"\"\n    request.session.clear()\n    request.session[\"user_id\"] = user[\"id\"]\n    csrf_token(request)\n\n\ndef end_session(request: Request) -> None:\n    request.session.clear()\n\n\nCSRF = Depends(check_csrf)\nSIGNED_IN = Depends(current_user)\nADMIN = Depends(admin_user)\n=== scripts/seed_demo.py\n#!/usr/bin/env python3\n\"\"\"Create demo data so a grader (and you) can use the CMS immediately.\n\n    uv run --env-file .env python scripts/seed_demo.py\n\nIt creates one admin and one editor (passwords read from the environment, never\nhard-coded), and, if there are no updates yet, a few sample updates: one\npublished and two drafts. Every sample says it is a sample and holds no score,\nso nothing invented can pass for a real result. Running it twice is harmless:\nexisting users and updates are kept.\n\nThe rubric expects this to run clean on a fresh clone with .env.example values\n(item E4), because the database itself is never committed.\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport os\nimport sys\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nsys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]))\n\nfrom app import db, settings, updates  # noqa: E402\nfrom app.users import DEMO_ADMIN, DEMO_EDITOR, seed_demo_users  # noqa: E402\n\n\n# (title, body, author email, published?)\nSAMPLE_UPDATES = [\n    (\"Welcome to the new team site (sample)\",\n     \"**This is sample content.** Real updates from the student media team will \"\n     \"appear here, newest first, each with the date it was last updated.\",\n     DEMO_ADMIN[\"email\"], True),\n    (\"Sample match report draft\",\n     \"**Sample draft.** A match report is written after a fixture and holds the \"\n     \"verified score and scorers. This one has neither.\",\n     DEMO_EDITOR[\"email\"], False),\n    (\"Sample preseason notes draft\",\n     \"**Sample draft.** Drafts stay in the admin console until the admin publishes them.\",\n     DEMO_EDITOR[\"email\"], False),\n]\n\n\ndef seed_sample_updates() -> int:\n    \"\"\"Add the sample updates if the database has none. Return how many were added.\"\"\"\n    if updates.list_updates():\n        return 0\n    with db.connect() as conn:\n        ids = {row[\"email\"]: row[\"id\"] for row in conn.execute(\"SELECT id, email FROM users\")}\n    for title, body, email, published in SAMPLE_UPDATES:\n        update_id = updates.create_update(title, body, ids[email])\n        if published:\n            updates.publish(update_id)\n    return len(SAMPLE_UPDATES)\n\n\ndef main() -> int:\n    admin_pw = os.environ.get(\"CMS_ADMIN_PASSWORD\")\n    editor_pw = os.environ.get(\"CMS_EDITOR_PASSWORD\")\n    if not admin_pw or not editor_pw:\n        print(\"Set CMS_ADMIN_PASSWORD and CMS_EDITOR_PASSWORD in .env \"\n              \"(copy .env.example).\")\n        return 1\n\n    created = seed_demo_users(admin_pw, editor_pw)\n    for person in (DEMO_ADMIN, DEMO_EDITOR):\n        state = \"created\" if person[\"email\"] in created else \"already exists\"\n        print(f\"{person['email']}: {state}\")\n    print(f\"Sample updates added: {seed_sample_updates()}\")\n    print(f\"Database: {settings.DATABASE_PATH}\")\n    return 0\n\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    sys.exit(main())\n\"\"\"T03: publish an update to the live site (issue #4).\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport re\nimport time\n\nimport pytest\nfrom fastapi.testclient import TestClient\n\nfrom app.main import create_app\nfrom app.publish import render_site\nfrom conftest import DEMO_USERS, create, csrf_token, login, visible\nfrom test_t02_updates HTTPException, Request\n\nfrom app import users\n\n\nclass LoginRequired(Exception):\n    \"\"\"Raised for an anonymous visitor; main.py turns it into a redirect.\"\"\"\n\n\nclass Refused(HTTPException):\n    \"\"\"A signed-in user tried something their role does not allow. main.py\n    shows the \"not allowed\" screen with this reason, as a 403.\"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self, reason: str):\n        super().__init__(status_code=403, detail=reason)\n\n\ndef csrf_token(request: Request) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Return this session's CSRF token, creating one if needed.\"\"\"\n    token = request.session.get(\"csrf_token\")\n    if not token:\n        token = secrets.token_urlsafe(32)\n        request.session[\"csrf_token\"] = token\n    return token\n\n\nasync def check_csrf(request: Request) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Dependency for every state-changing route: reject a missing or wrong token.\"\"\"\n    form = await request.form()\n    sent = form.get(\"csrf_token\")\n    expected = request.session.get(\"csrf_token\")\n    if not (isinstance(sent, str) and expected\n            and hmac.compare_digest(sent, expected)):\n        raise HTTPException(status_code=403, detail=\"Invalid or missing CSRF token\")\n\n\ndef signed_in_user(request: Request) -> sqlite3.Row | None:\n    \"\"\"The signed-in, still-active user, or None.\"\"\"\n    user_id = request.session.get(\"user_id\")\n    return users.get_active_user(user_id) if user_id else None\n\n\ndef current_user(request: Request) -> sqlite3.Row:\n    \"\"\"Dependency for every admin screen: the signed-in, still-active user.\"\"\"\n    user = signed_in_user(request)\n    if user is None:\n        request.session.pop(\"user_id\", None)\n        raise LoginRequired\n    return user\n\n\ndef admin_user(user: sqlite3.Row = Depends(current_user)) -> sqlite3.Row:\n    \"\"\"Dependency for admin-only actions: an editor is refused with 403.\"\"\"\n    if user[\"role\"] != \"admin\":\n        raise Refused(\"Only the admin can do this.\")\n    return user\n\n\ndef start_session(request: Request, user: sqlite3.Row) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Begin a fresh session for the user, with a new CSRF token.\"\"\"\n    request.session.clear()\n    request.session[\"user_id\"] = user[\"id\"]\n    csrf_token(request)\n\n\ndef end_session(request: Request) -> None:\n    request.session.clear()\n\n\nCSRF = Depends(check_csrf)\nSIGNED_IN = Depends(current_user)\nADMIN = Depends(admin_user)\n=== scripts/seed_demo.py\n#!/usr/bin/env python3\n\"\"\"Create demo data so a grader (and you) can use the CMS immediately.\n\n    uv run --env-file .env python scripts/seed_demo.py\n\nIt creates one admin and one editor (passwords read from the environment, never\nhard-coded), and, if there are no updates yet, a few sample updates: one\npublished and two drafts. Every sample says it is a sample and holds no score,\nso nothing invented can pass for a real result. Running it twice is harmless:\nexisting users and updates are kept.\n\nThe rubric expects this to run clean on a fresh clone with .env.example values\n(item E4), because the database itself is never committed.\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport os\nimport sys\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nsys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]))\n\nfrom app import db, settings, updates  # noqa: E402\nfrom app.users import DEMO_ADMIN, DEMO_EDITOR, seed_demo_users  # noqa: E402\n\n\n# (title, body, author email, published?)\nSAMPLE_UPDATES = [\n    (\"Welcome to the new team site (sample)\",\n     \"**This is sample content.** Real updates from the student media team will \"\n     \"appear here, newest first, each with the date it was last updated.\",\n     DEMO_ADMIN[\"email\"], True),\n    (\"Sample match report draft\",\n     \"**Sample draft.** A match report is written after a fixture and holds the \"\n     \"verified score and scorers. This one has neither.\",\n     DEMO_EDITOR[\"email\"], False),\n    (\"Sample preseason notes draft\",\n     \"**Sample draft.** Drafts stay in the admin console until the admin publishes them.\",\n     DEMO_EDITOR[\"email\"], False),\n]\n\n\ndef seed_sample_updates() -> int:\n    \"\"\"Add the sample updates if the database has none. Return how many were added.\"\"\"\n    if updates.list_updates():\n        return 0\n    with db.connect() as conn:\n        ids = {row[\"email\"]: row[\"id\"] for row in conn.execute(\"SELECT id, email FROM users\")}\n    for title, body, email, published in SAMPLE_UPDATES:\n        update_id = updates.create_update(title, body, ids[email])\n        if published:\n            updates.publish(update_id)\n    return len(SAMPLE_UPDATES)\n\n\ndef main() -> int:\n    admin_pw = os.environ.get(\"CMS_ADMIN_PASSWORD\")\n    editor_pw = os.environ.get(\"CMS_EDITOR_PASSWORD\")\n    if not admin_pw or not editor_pw:\n        print(\"Set CMS_ADMIN_PASSWORD and CMS_EDITOR_PASSWORD in .env \"\n              \"(copy .env.example).\")\n        return 1\n\n    created = seed_demo_users(admin_pw, editor_pw)\n    for person in (DEMO_ADMIN, DEMO_EDITOR):\n        state = \"created\" if person[\"email\"] in created else \"already exists\"\n        print(f\"{person['email']}: {state}\")\n    print(f\"Sample updates added: {seed_sample_updates()}\")\n    print(f\"Database: {settings.DATABASE_PATH}\")\n    return 0\n\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    sys.exit(main())\n\"\"\"T03: publish an update to the live site (issue #4).\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport re\nimport time\n\nimport pytest\nfrom client.post(f\"{url}/{verb}\", data={\"csrf_token\": csrf_token(client, url)},\n                       follow_redirects=False)\n\n\ndef url, \"publish\")\n    assert response.status_code == 303 and response.headers[\"location\"] == url\n\n    restarted = TestClient(create_app())\n    login(restarted, DEMO_USERS[\"admin\"][\"email\"], client_as(\"admin\")\n    url = create(admin, \"Pulled (sample)\")\n    post_status_form(admin, url, \"publish\")\n    assert post_status_form(admin, url, \"unpublish\").status_code == 303\n\n    restarted = TestClient(create_app())\n    login(restarted, DEMO_USERS[\"admin\"][\"email\"], DEMO_USERS[\"admin\"][\"password\"])\n    assert \"Status: Draft\" in visible(restarted.get(url).text)\n\n\n@pytest.mark.parametrize(\"verb,start,after\", [\n    (\"publish\", \"Draft\", \"Draft\"), (\"unpublish\", \"Published\", \"Published\"),\n])\ndef test_editor_cannot_publish_or_unpublish(client_as, verb, start, after):\n    admin, editor = client_as(\"admin\"), client_as(\"editor\")\n    url = create(admin, \"Admin only (sample)\")\n    if start \"original-title\"\n## Problem Statement\n\nKenyon College Men's Soccer has no reliable place for fans, alumni, and players' families to find accurate game information. Today news comes through Instagram, which is hard to search and confusing for older relatives, and updates arrive in a random order. The team's student media members have average computer skills and need a simple way to write updates, but a wrong score or scorer on a public team site is worse than no site at all. The program needs a small CMS where several students can prepare content, one trusted person decides what goes public, and fans see a fast, readable, purple and white site that says when it was last updated.\n\n## Solution\n\nA local admin console (FastAPI, Jinja, SQLite) where one admin and a group of student editors log in, write updates and pages, and manage users, plus a `cms publish` step that exports only published content as static HTML for GitHub Pages. Editors can only produce drafts; the single admin reviews and publishes. The public site shows the newest updates on the home page, a navigation built from published pages (Schedule, Roster, Results/Record, History, About/Contact), and a last-updated date on everything. The admin console never goes on the internet.\n\n## User Stories\n\n1. As an editor, I want to log in with my own email and password, so that my work is attributed to me.\n2. As an editor, I want a clear message when my password is wrong, so that I know to retry rather than think the site is broken.\n3. As an admin, I want to log out, so that nobody else can use the shared machine under my name.\n4. As an editor, I want to log out, so that the next editor at the shared machine signs in as themselves.\n5. As an admin, I want every password stored only as a hash, so that a stolen database never reveals passwords.\n6. As an editor, I want to create an update with a title and a Markdown body, so that I can write up a game quickly.\n7. As an editor, I want the slug generated from the title automatically, so that I never have to think about URLs.\n8. As an editor, I want a duplicate slug to be resolved automatically, so that two updates with the same title do not collide.\n9. As an editor, I want a Markdown preview in the editor, so that I can check formatting before I save.\n10. As an editor, I want my new content saved as a draft, so that nothing reaches fans before the admin approves it.\n11. As an editor, I want to edit any draft, so that a teammate can fix a mistake on game night.\n12. As an editor, I want to delete my own drafts, so that abandoned drafts do not clutter the list.\n13. As an editor, I want to be blocked from deleting someone else's draft, so that nobody loses work by accident.\n14. As an editor, I want to be blocked from publishing, unpublishing, or editing published content, so that live content only changes with the admin's approval.\n15. As an editor, I want a clear \"not allowed\" screen when I try an admin-only action, so that I understand why it did not work.\n16. As an editor, I want to create and edit page drafts such as Schedule, Roster, or History, so that I can prepare content for the admin.\n17. As an editor, I want to filter the content list by status and by type, so that I can find drafts that need work.\n18. As an editor, I want a success or error message after every save, so that I know whether my change landed.\n19. As an editor, I want the admin navigation visible on every screen, so that I never get lost.\n20. As an admin, I want a dashboard showing counts of drafts, published updates, and pages, so that I see what needs review at a glance.\n21. As an admin, I want to filter the content list to drafts, so that I can review what editors wrote.\n22. As an admin, I want to publish a draft, so that it becomes eligible for the public site.\n23. As an admin, I want to unpublish published content, so that a wrong score can be pulled quickly.\n24. As an admin, I want to edit published content, so that I can correct a mistake.\n25. As an admin, I want to delete published content or pages, with a confirm step, so that I do not remove something live by accident.\n26. As an admin, I want to set each page's nav order, so that Schedule and Results appear before History and About.\n27. As an admin, I want to create a user with an email, a name, a role, and a starting password, so that a new media member can join.\n28. As an admin, I want to change a user's role, so that responsibilities can change.\n29. As an admin, I want to deactivate a user, so that a graduating media member can no longer log in.\n30. As a deactivated user, I want my past drafts and attribution kept, so that history is not rewritten.\n31. As an admin, I want the system to enforce exactly one admin, so that the club's single-admin rule is true in code.\n32. As an admin, I want a hand-over action that promotes another user and demotes me in one step, so that the role can pass on when I graduate.\n33. As an admin, I want to be prevented from deactivating or demoting myself outside of hand-over, so that the site is never left without an admin.\n34. As an admin, I want `cms publish` to render only published updates and pages, so that drafts never leave the database.\n35. As an admin, I want `cms publish` to remove content I unpublished or deleted from the exported site, so that stale content does not stay live.\n36. As an admin, I want `cms deploy` to push the export to the gh-pages branch, so that fans see the new content.\n37. As an admin, I want a short written runbook for publish and deploy, so that whoever inherits the role can do it.\n38. As a fan, I want the home page to list the newest published updates first with their dates, so that I see the latest news.\n39. As a fan, I want a navigation menu built from published pages, so that I can reach Schedule, Roster, Results, History, and About.\n40. As a fan, I want each update and page to show when it was last updated, so that I can judge whether it is current.\n41. As a fan, I want to read a match report with the verified score and scorers, so that I trust the numbers.\n42. As an alumnus, I want a History page about past titles and accomplishments, so that I can find the program's record.\n43. As a player's relative, I want a Roster page, so that I can find the player.\n44. As a fan on a phone, I want the public site and admin screens to fit without sideways scrolling, so that I can read them anywhere.\n45. As a fan, I want the site to look purple and white with a clear header, so that it feels like Kenyon.\n46. As any visitor, I want all links to work on the hosted site, so that I never hit a broken page.\n47. As any visitor, I want no script from a user's Markdown to run, so that the site is safe to open.\n48. As the admin, I want every state-changing form to carry a CSRF token, so that another website cannot act on my behalf.\n49. As a maintainer, I want sample content clearly marked as sample, so that no invented score ever looks real.\n50. As an anonymous visitor to the admin console, I want to be sent to the login page, so that nothing is exposed.\n\n## Implementation Decisions\n\n- **Architecture.** Follow ADR-001 and ADR-002: a local FastAPI app with server-rendered Jinja templates and SQLite, and a publish step that writes static HTML. No frontend framework and no build step.\n- **Vocabulary.** All code, templates, and tickets use the terms in `CONTEXT.md`: Update (stored as a post), Fixture, Match report, Page, Nav order, Draft, Published, Slug, Admin, Editor, Hand-over, Last updated.\n- **Users.** A user has an email, a display name, a password hash (argon2), a role (admin or editor), and an active flag. Deactivation sets the flag and never deletes the user, so authorship survives.\n- **Single admin.** Exactly one active admin exists at all times. Role changes cannot create a second admin, and the admin cannot demote or deactivate themselves. The only path is a hand-over action, which promotes the target and demotes the current admin atomically.\n- **Content.** Updates and Pages share the same core fields: title, slug, Markdown body, status (draft or published), author, created and updated timestamps. Pages add a nav order. Only two statuses exist.\n- **Slugs.** Generated from the title on first save, made unique automatically, and not editable by editors. Only the admin may change a slug.\n- **Permissions.** Editor: create content as drafts, edit any draft, delete own drafts, view the content list and dashboard. Editor may not publish, unpublish, edit or delete published content, delete another editor's draft, or reach user management. Admin: everything, including publish, unpublish, edit and delete published content, and user management. Admin-only routes return 403 for editors and redirect anonymous visitors to login.\n- **Session and login.** Cookie-based sessions. Login failures show one generic message. Deactivated users cannot log in.\n- **CSRF.** Every state-changing form carries a token that the server verifies, and a POST without a valid token is rejected.\n- **Markdown safety.** User Markdown is rendered and then sanitized with an allow-list, both in the admin preview and in the export, so script tags and event-handler attributes never execute.\n- **Admin console.** A dashboard with counts, a filterable content list (by status and by type), an editor with a Markdown preview, a user list, and persistent navigation. Every save shows a success or error message. The console is not themed beyond clear, plain styling.\n- **Publish.** `cms publish` reads only published rows and regenerates the export folder from scratch, so unpublished or deleted content disappears. Output uses relative paths only. The home page lists published updates newest first, the navigation is built from published pages by nav order, and each item shows its last-updated date. `cms deploy` pushes the export to the gh-pages branch. Both commands run from the terminal, and a short runbook is part of the documentation.\n- **Public look.** Purple and white, with a CSS-only banner header, readable at 390 px. No image files are required.\n- **Seed data.** The demo seed creates one admin, one editor, a few drafts, and a few published items. All content is clearly marked as sample, never realistic scores or stats. Credentials come from the environment.\n- **Assumptions.** A deactivated user keeps authorship and content. Updates are expected about an hour after a game. Editors use one shared machine for now.\n\n## Testing Decisions\n\n- **What a good test is.** It asserts external behavior only: a status code, a redirect, a page's visible text, a file in the export. It never asserts on internal functions, table layouts, or template structure.\n- **Seam 1: the HTTP app.** Every capability is tested through the FastAPI test client, using the existing `client` and `client_as(role)` helpers. This covers login and logout, roles and the editor 403 and anonymous redirect on every admin-only route, content CRUD and status changes, the dashboard and filters, preview, user management, hand-over, CSRF rejection, and sanitized preview output.\n- **Seam 2: the publish export.** Run the exporter into a temporary folder and assert on the generated files: only published content is present, drafts are absent, unpublished content disappears on re-export, no root-absolute paths, navigation order matches nav order, sanitized bodies, and a last-updated date on each item.\n- **Acceptance criteria.** Each ticket's acceptance criteria map to at least one named test so the review and grading can trace them.\n- **Prior art.** The template's existing T00 test and the `client_as` fixture and its docstring examples for access-control tests.\n- **Not tested.** Visual styling and the GitHub deploy itself are checked by hand and with screenshots at 1280 px and 390 px.\n\n## Out of Scope\n\n- Comments and moderation.\n- Live in-game scores or any server-side feature on the public site.\n- WYSIWYG editors, drag-and-drop page builders, and multi-site.\n- Remote access for editors; for now the console runs on one machine (a later change, possibly the live admin deploy stretch).\n- A \"verified result\" workflow or required source field for scores.\n- Theming the admin console.\n- Photo uploads and categories/tags are wanted but not in the core build; see Further Notes.\n\n## Further Notes\n\n- **Stretch goals, after the 7 core capabilities are green and reviewed:** photo uploads with alt text, and categories and tags (for example by season or opponent). Each gets its own `stretch` issue. Each is worth 1 extra-credit point and only counts if the base score is 70 or higher.\n- **Core ticket plan.** The 7 required capabilities should split into 7 to 9 vertical tickets, each demoable alone and touching data, route, template, and test.\n- **Accuracy rule.** The client's hard rule is that the site must never show false information. That is the reason for draft-only editors, a last-updated date, clearly marked sample content, and unpublish being fast for the admin.\n- **ADR candidate.** Enforcing exactly one admin may be recorded as an ADR; this is pending the author's decision.\n- **Open item outside this spec.** `notes/cms-field-notes.md` needs at least 5 observations from WordPress Playground (S1.1) before Stage 1.\n# Pinned skills\n\nInstall the mattpocock engineering skills into this repo, then configure them\nonce. visible(export(tmp_path)[\"index.html\"])\n    assert home.index(\"Newer sample\") < home.index(\"Older sample corrected\")\n\n\ndef last_updated(html: str) -> str:\n    return re.search(r'Updated <time datetime=\"([^\"]+)\"', html).group(1)\n\n\ndef test_publishing_sets_the_last_updated_time(client_as):\n    \"\"\"A fan judging freshness sees when the update went live, not when it was drafted.\"\"\"\n    admin = client_as(\"admin\")\n    url = create(admin, \"Drafted earlier (sample)\")\n    drafted = last_updated(admin.get(url).text)\n    time.sleep(1.1)\n    post_status_form(admin, url, \"publish\")\n    assert last_updated(admin.get(url).text) > drafted\n\"\"\"T02: admin writes update drafts (issue #3).\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport re\n\nimport pytest\nfrom fastapi.testclient import TestClient\n\nfrom app.main import create_app\nfrom conftest import DEMO_USERS, NEW, create, csrf_token, login, save_new, visible\n\ndef slug_on(html: str) -> str:\n    return re.search(r\"Slug: (\\S+)\", visible(html)).group(1)\n\n\ndef save_edit(client: TestClient, url: str, title: str, body: str = \"\", **extra):\n    data = {\"title\": title, \"body\": body, \"csrf_token\": csrf_token(client, url), **extra}\n    return client.post(url, data=data, follow_redirects=False)\n\n\ndef test_admin_creates_a_draft_with_author_and_timestamps(client_as):\n    admin = client_as(\"admin\")\n    url = create(admin, \"Lords beat Denison\", \"A **good** night.\")\n\n    page = admin.get(url)\n    assert page.status_code == 200\n    assert 'value=\"Lords beat Denison\"' in page.text\n    text = visible(page.text)\n    assert \"Status: Draft\" in text\n    assert \"Author: Sample Admin\" in text\n    assert re.search(r\"Created \\d{4}-\\d\\d-\\d\\d \\d\\d:\\d\\d\", text)\n    assert re.search(r\"Updated \\d{4}-\\d\\d-\\d\\d \\d\\d:\\d\\d\", text)\n\n    listing = admin.get(\"/admin/updates\").text\n    assert \"Lords beat Denison\" in listing and \"Draft\" in listing\n\n\ndef test_new_updates_are_drafts_even_if_the_form_says_published(client_as):\n    admin = client_as(\"admin\")\n    url = create(admin, \"Sneaky\", \"\")\n    save_edit(admin, url, \"Sneaky\", \"\", status=\"published\")\n    assert \"Status: Draft\" in visible(admin.get(url).text)\n\n\ndef test_slug_comes_from_title_and_stays_unique(client_as):\n    admin = client_as(\"admin\")\n    first = admin.get(create(admin, \"Lords Beat Denison 2–1!\")).text\n    second = admin.get(create(admin, \"Lords Beat Denison 2–1!\")).text\n    slugs = [slug_on(page) for page in (first, second)]\n    assert slugs[0] == \"lords-beat-denison-2-1\"\n    assert slugs[1] != slugs[0] and slugs[1].startswith(\"lords-beat-denison-2-1\")\n\n\ndef test_slug_does_not_change_when_the_title_is_edited(client_as):\n    admin = client_as(\"admin\")\n    url = create(admin, \"Original title\")\n    save_edit(admin, url, \"A new title\")\n    page = admin.get(url).text\n    assert 'value=\"A new title\"' in page\n    assert slug_on(page) == \"original-title\"\n## Problem Statement\n\nKenyon College Men's Soccer has no reliable place for fans, alumni, and players' families to find accurate game information. Today news comes through Instagram, which is hard to search and confusing for older relatives, and updates arrive in a random order. The team's student media members have average computer skills and need a simple way to write updates, but a wrong score or scorer on a public team site is worse than no site at all. The program needs a small CMS where several students can prepare content, one trusted person decides what goes public, and fans see a fast, readable, purple and white site that says when it was last updated.\n\n## Solution\n\nA local admin console (FastAPI, Jinja, SQLite) where one admin and a group of student editors log in, write updates and pages, and manage users, plus a `cms publish` step that exports only published content as static HTML for GitHub Pages. Editors can only produce drafts; the single admin reviews and publishes. The public site shows the newest updates on the home page, a navigation built from published pages (Schedule, Roster, Results/Record, History, About/Contact), and a last-updated date on everything. The admin console never goes on the internet.\n\n## User Stories\n\n1. As an editor, I want to log in with my own email and password, so that my work is attributed to me.\n2. As an editor, I want a clear message when my password is wrong, so that I know to retry rather than think the site is broken.\n3. As an admin, I want to log out, so that nobody else can use the shared machine under my name.\n4. As an editor, I want to log out, so that the next editor at the shared machine signs in as themselves.\n5. As an admin, I want every password stored only as a hash, so that a stolen database never reveals passwords.\n6. As an editor, I want to create an update with a title and a Markdown body, so that I can write up a game quickly.\n7. As an editor, I want the slug generated from the title automatically, so that I never have to think about URLs.\n8. As an editor, I want a duplicate slug to be resolved automatically, so that two updates with the same title do not collide.\n9. As an editor, I want a Markdown preview in the editor, so that I can check formatting before I save.\n10. As an editor, I want my new content saved as a draft, so that nothing reaches fans before the admin approves it.\n11. As an editor, I want to edit any draft, so that a teammate can fix a mistake on game night.\n12. As an editor, I want to delete my own drafts, so that abandoned drafts do not clutter the list.\n13. As an editor, I want to be blocked from deleting someone else's draft, so that nobody loses work by accident.\n14. As an editor, I want to be blocked from publishing, unpublishing, or editing published content, so that live content only changes with the admin's approval.\n15. As an editor, I want a clear \"not allowed\" screen when I try an admin-only action, so that I understand why it did not work.\n16. As an editor, I want to create and edit page drafts such as Schedule, Roster, or History, so that I can prepare content for the admin.\n17. As an editor, I want to filter the content list by status and by type, so that I can find drafts that need work.\n18. As an editor, I want a success or error message after every save, so that I know whether my change landed.\n19. As an editor, I want the admin navigation visible on every screen, so that I never get lost.\n20. As an admin, I want a dashboard showing counts of drafts, published updates, and pages, so that I see what needs review at a glance.\n21. As an admin, I want to filter the content list to drafts, so that I can review what editors wrote.\n22. As an admin, I want to publish a draft, so that it becomes eligible for the public site.\n23. As an admin, I want to unpublish published content, so that a wrong score can be pulled quickly.\n24. As an admin, I want to edit published content, so that I can correct a mistake.\n25. As an admin, I want to delete published content or pages, with a confirm step, so that I do not remove something live by accident.\n26. As an admin, I want to set each page's nav order, so that Schedule and Results appear before History and About.\n27. As an admin, I want to create a user with an email, a name, a role, and a starting password, so that a new media member can join.\n28. As an admin, I want to change a user's role, so that responsibilities can change.\n29. As an admin, I want to deactivate a user, so that a graduating media member can no longer log in.\n30. As a deactivated user, I want my past drafts and attribution kept, so that history is not rewritten.\n31. As an admin, I want the system to enforce exactly one admin, so that the club's single-admin rule is true in code.\n32. As an admin, I want a hand-over action that promotes another user and demotes me in one step, so that the role can pass on when I graduate.\n33. As an admin, I want to be prevented from deactivating or demoting myself outside of hand-over, so that the site is never left without an admin.\n34. As an admin, I want `cms publish` to render only published updates and pages, so that drafts never leave the database.\n35. As an admin, I want `cms publish` to remove content I unpublished or deleted from the exported site, so that stale content does not stay live.\n36. As an admin, I want `cms deploy` to push the export to the gh-pages branch, so that fans see the new content.\n37. As an admin, I want a short written runbook for publish and deploy, so that whoever inherits the role can do it.\n38. As a fan, I want the home page to list the newest published updates first with their dates, so that I see the latest news.\n39. As a fan, I want a navigation menu built from published pages, so that I can reach Schedule, Roster, Results, History, and About.\n40. As a fan, I want each update and page to show when it was last updated, so that I can judge whether it is current.\n41. As a fan, I want to read a match report with the verified score and scorers, so that I trust the numbers.\n42. As an alumnus, I want a History page about past titles and accomplishments, so that I can find the program's record.\n43. As a player's relative, I want a Roster page, so that I can find the player.\n44. As a fan on a phone, I want the public site and admin screens to fit without sideways scrolling, so that I can read them anywhere.\n45. As a fan, I want the site to look purple and white with a clear header, so that it feels like Kenyon.\n46. As any visitor, I want all links to work on the hosted site, so that I never hit a broken page.\n47. As any visitor, I want no script from a user's Markdown to run, so that the site is safe to open.\n48. As the admin, I want every state-changing form to carry a CSRF token, so that another website cannot act on my behalf.\n49. As a maintainer, I want sample content clearly marked as sample, so that no invented score ever looks real.\n50. As an anonymous visitor to the admin console, I want to be sent to the login page, so that nothing is exposed.\n\n## Implementation Decisions\n\n- **Architecture.** Follow ADR-001 and ADR-002: a local FastAPI app with server-rendered Jinja templates and SQLite, and a publish step that writes static HTML. No frontend framework and no build step.\n- **Vocabulary.** All code, templates, and tickets use the terms in `CONTEXT.md`: Update (stored as a post), Fixture, Match report, Page, Nav order, Draft, Published, Slug, Admin, Editor, Hand-over, Last updated.\n- **Users.** A user has an email, a display name, a password hash (argon2), a role (admin or editor), and an active flag. Deactivation sets the flag and never deletes the user, so authorship survives.\n- **Single admin.** Exactly one active admin exists at all times. Role changes cannot create a second admin, and the admin cannot demote or deactivate themselves. The only path is a hand-over action, which promotes the target and demotes the current admin atomically.\n- **Content.** Updates and Pages share the same core fields: title, slug, Markdown body, status (draft or published), author, created and updated timestamps. Pages add a nav order. Only two statuses exist.\n- **Slugs.** Generated from the title on first save, made unique automatically, and not editable by editors. Only the admin may change a slug.\n- **Permissions.** Editor: create content as drafts, edit any draft, delete own drafts, view the content list and dashboard. Editor may not publish, unpublish, edit or delete published content, delete another editor's draft, or reach user management. Admin: everything, including publish, unpublish, edit and delete published content, and user management. Admin-only routes return 403 for editors and redirect anonymous visitors to login.\n- **Session and login.** Cookie-based sessions. Login failures show one generic message. Deactivated users cannot log in.\n- **CSRF.** Every state-changing form carries a token that the server verifies, and a POST without a valid token is rejected.\n- **Markdown safety.** User Markdown is rendered and then sanitized with an allow-list, both in the admin preview and in the export, so script tags and event-handler attributes never execute.\n- **Admin console.** A dashboard with counts, a filterable content list (by status and by type), an editor with a Markdown preview, a user list, and persistent navigation. Every save shows a success or error message. The console is not themed beyond clear, plain styling.\n- **Publish.** `cms publish` reads only published rows and regenerates the export folder from scratch, so unpublished or deleted content disappears. Output uses relative paths only. The home page lists published updates newest first, the navigation is built from published pages by nav order, and each item shows its last-updated date. `cms deploy` pushes the export to the gh-pages branch. Both commands run from the terminal, and a short runbook is part of the documentation.\n- **Public look.** Purple and white, with a CSS-only banner header, readable at 390 px. No image files are required.\n- **Seed data.** The demo seed creates one admin, one editor, a few drafts, and a few published items. All content is clearly marked as sample, never realistic scores or stats. Credentials come from the environment.\n- **Assumptions.** A deactivated user keeps authorship and content. Updates are expected about an hour after a game. Editors use one shared machine for now.\n\n## Testing Decisions\n\n- **What a good test is.** It asserts external behavior only: a status code, a redirect, a page's visible text, a file in the export. It never asserts on internal functions, table layouts, or template structure.\n- **Seam 1: the HTTP app.** Every capability is tested through the FastAPI test client, using the existing `client` and `client_as(role)` helpers. This covers login and logout, roles and the editor 403 and anonymous redirect on every admin-only route, content CRUD and status changes, the dashboard and filters, preview, user management, hand-over, CSRF rejection, and sanitized preview output.\n- **Seam 2: the publish export.** Run the exporter into a temporary folder and assert on the generated files: only published content is present, drafts are absent, unpublished content disappears on re-export, no root-absolute paths, navigation order matches nav order, sanitized bodies, and a last-updated date on each item.\n- **Acceptance criteria.** Each ticket's acceptance criteria map to at least one named test so the review and grading can trace them.\n- **Prior art.** The template's existing T00 test and the `client_as` fixture and its docstring examples for access-control tests.\n- **Not tested.** Visual styling and the GitHub deploy itself are checked by hand and with screenshots at 1280 px and 390 px.\n\n## Out of Scope\n\n- Comments and moderation.\n- Live in-game scores or any server-side feature on the public site.\n- WYSIWYG editors, drag-and-drop page builders, and multi-site.\n- Remote access for editors; for now the console runs on one machine (a later change, possibly the live admin deploy stretch).\n- A \"verified result\" workflow or required source field for scores.\n- Theming the admin console.\n- Photo uploads and categories/tags are wanted but not in the core build; see Further Notes.\n\n## Further Notes\n\n- **Stretch goals, after the 7 core capabilities are green and reviewed:** photo uploads with alt text, and categories and tags (for example by season or opponent). Each gets its own `stretch` issue. Each is worth 1 extra-credit point and only counts if the base score is 70 or higher.\n- **Core ticket plan.** The 7 required capabilities should split into 7 to 9 vertical tickets, each demoable alone and touching data, route, template, and test.\n- **Accuracy rule.** The client's hard rule is that the site must never show false information. That is the reason for draft-only editors, a last-updated date, clearly marked sample content, and unpublish being fast for the admin.\n- **ADR candidate.** Enforcing exactly one admin may be recorded as an ADR; this is pending the author's decision.\n- **Open item outside this spec.** `notes/cms-field-notes.md` needs at least 5 observations from WordPress Playground (S1.1) before Stage 1.\n# Pinned skills\n\nInstall the mattpocock engineering skills into this repo, then configure them\nonce. Everyone in the class uses the same version, so the manual's commands match\nwhat you see.\n\n```bash\nnpx skills@latest add mattpocock/skills\nclaude\n# then, inside Claude Code:\n/setup-matt-pocock-skills      # tracker: GitHub · labels: defaults · docs: single context\n```\n\nThe flow you will use: `/grill-with-docs → /to-spec → /to-tickets → /implement → /code-review`.\nHelp commands: `/ask-matt` (which skill fits), `/wait-what` (that did not land),\n`/teach` (learn a topic across sessions).\n\n**Name clash:** this set ships its own `/teach`, which is not the `/teach` you\nwrote in Week 4. If you want yours here, copy it to\n`.claude/skills/teach-log/SKILL.md` and rename it inside the file.\n\n**Record the version you installed** in `notes/setup_check.md`:\n\n```bash\nclaude --version >> notes/setup_check.md\nls .claude/skills >> notes/setup_check.md\n```","stderr":"","interrupted":false,"isImage":false,"noOutputExpected":false},"serverClassifierContext":{"request":"bc6683f1-e12e-4b15-8302-d11f139623b2","context":{"git_state":{"cwd":"/Users/maysg/orca/iphs400-mp2-cms","root":"/Users/maysg/orca/iphs400-mp2-cms","branch":"main","default_branch":"main","status":{"clean":false,"counts":{"staged":0,"modified":1,"untracked":null,"untracked_normal":1},"porcelain":null,"truncated":false},"visibility":{"origin":{"host":"github.com","remote":"MaysG-creator/iphs400-mp2-cms","visibility":"public"},"push_remote":"origin","remotes":[{"name":"origin","host":"github.com","remote":"MaysG-creator/iphs400-mp2-cms","visibility":"public"}],"visibility_cache":[{"host":"github.com","remote":"MaysG-creator/iphs400-mp2-cms","visibility":"public"}]}},"live_cwd":"/Users/maysg/orca/iphs400-mp2-cms","platform":"macos"}},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"1d5de221-8789-43cc-87cc-23ffc8f753d4","permissionDecision":{"decision":"accept","source":"config","reasonType":"classifier"},"session_id":"a121db57-1bee-4dbb-8856-8744e70c4142","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/Users/maysg/orca/iphs400-mp2-cms","sessionId":"afcf6f29-4133-4319-8044-e192682b7663","version":"2.1.296","gitBranch":"main"}
